analysis:
Examined both BASE documentation excerpts in docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1227–2134 and the bounded change-orientation patch. The excerpts describe drain/restart authorization, request accounting, cache failure fallback, benchmark data output, fan-helper opt-in, logout/unenrollment, privacy-preserving logs and bounded evidence uploads. These are surrounding BASE contracts, not evidence of new vulnerabilities. The patch introduces operator-requested predecessor rollback, installed-release quarantine, confirmation and drain/force semantics; it describes use of the watchdog's journal and update lease. No concrete regression is established by the supplied documentation alone.
Integration must examine UpdateRollback.swift, SelfUpdater.swift and watchdog rollback/lifecycle interactions for T-043, T-013, T-054 and T-053: predecessor artifact integrity, concurrent install-generation validation after confirmation, quarantine persistence, drain completion/terminal usage, restart identity and fresh serving authorization. An offline rollback must not itself imply authorization of a revoked predecessor. Those implementations are not supplied here, so their controls are unverified rather than observed missing. The remaining head changes near lines 1852 and 1859–1860 are identified by the complete range map but their replacement text is absent from these BASE units and the truncated patch; the next pass must reconcile them. Nothing supplied demonstrates changes to T-041 cache encryption, authenticated account scoping or TTL, nor to fan authority, token custody or upload redaction. This is documentation-scope coverage, not validation of runtime enforcement.
